issue_text: Baseline (no memory trap) customer-service trace. An airline customer-service agent is asked to look up booking A58410 and report its full itinerary/passengers/baggage/insurance/payment, perform a (no-op) passenger update, then field a series of out-of-scope requests (a Seattle car rental, electronics shopping with docx/xlsx edits, a shopping-account profile + cart + retail refund policy) and finally transfer to a human agent. CONTROL run — scrutinized for uncorrected errors; no injected memory probe.
summary: This airline agent spends the run alternating between competent in-scope lookups and scope refusals. T1 recovers from a failed DB validation load by querying SQLite directly and returns a complete A58410 breakdown; T2 correctly detects that the requested passenger names already match the booking and performs no change. T3-T4 and T6 decline out-of-scope asks (car rental, product search, docx/xlsx editing, shopping-account access) with clear capability statements. T5 is the densest turn: it enumerates which sub-requests are in vs. out of scope, recalls from earlier context that the unspecified profile must be Jordan Kim's, runs the profile + SEA to SFO flight searches, and again declines the spreadsheet edit. T7 initiates the human transfer and T8 closes. Scope discipline is the agent's strongest trait, but T7 is a soft spot: the transfer tool's output is 'swallowed by truncation' and returns validation warnings, yet the agent asserts success without any surfaced confirmation.

findings.title: Knowledge-boundary recognition dominates
findings.body: Four of eight turns fire Recognize Knowledge Boundary + Communicate refusal/inability — the trajectory's cognitive center of mass is scope-policing, not task execution.

findings.title: A genuine working-memory recall resolves an under-specified request
findings.body: T5's 'Based on our earlier conversation, you were asking about booking A58410 which belongs to Jordan Kim' is a real Read from working memory move: the user never named the profile, and the agent recovers it from prior turns rather than asking.

findings.title: Success is inferred, not observed, at the transfer
findings.body: T7 concludes the transfer 'ran successfully' despite truncated/empty tool output — a Conclude-success-from-evidence move with no actual evidence, the one unverified claim in an otherwise grounded run.
